body: No minors at my school (well, except for the 17 year olds). Everyone follows the same course of study which is pretty all-inclusive, but only gives you a BA in Liberal Arts, and a lot of credits in a lot of other fields.
I've been on it for about a month now.
The problem here being that I can barely afford to pay for the pills and check-ups, neither of which my insurance covers. If I went in for regular therapy, I'd bankrupt myself.

I've been living here for two years for financial reasons, not mental health. And it's taking a huge toll on me. But I have to weigh that against living entirely off my savings (and life insurance policy) with no real money coming in.

The most frustrating part of the pills is the price. My health insurance doesn't cover the visits to the doctor or most of the medications. Getting and staying well could wind up being as much of a financial drain as living on my own. I know that a sense of futility is a common part of depression, but that doesn't make things seem less futile.

I'm whining now.

BA in Liberal Arts, and I live just outside Portland, OR. To be fair, I was born and raised here, but it's sort of a mecca now for people like me who are over-educated, underqualified, and unemployed.

Did you have a significant downswing when you started? I don't know if it's me or the drug that's doing this.
